title: The billing PR added a PATCH /api/subscription endpoint that takes the target customer's email from a query parameter instead of the logged-in user, so any authenticated user can cancel or resume anyone's Stripe subscription.

findings.explanation: All database queries in the diff use Django ORM's filter() with keyword arguments, which are parameterized automatically. No raw SQL or string-interpolated queries are used. User-supplied values (email, file_source, etc.) are passed as ORM filter parameters, not interpolated into raw SQL strings.

The set_user_subscription() and get_user_subscription() functions look up and modify subscription records purely by email address. If the caller of these functions is a webhook or API endpoint that does not verify the email belongs to the authenticated caller (e.g., a billing webhook trusting a payload email field without signature verification or ownership check), an attacker could manipulate another user's subscription. Without seeing the subscription_router implementation (referenced in configure.py but not included in the diff), it is impossible to confirm whether proper authorization is enforced before these adapters are called.

evidence.content:
from khoj.routers.subscription import subscription_router
    ...
    if state.billing_enabled:
        logger.info("💳 Enabled Billing")
        app.include_router(subscription_router, prefix="/api/subscription")

findings.suggested_fix: Ensure that set_user_subscription() is only callable from a route that either: (a) verifies the request comes from a trusted billing provider via webhook signature verification, or (b) restricts email modification to the currently authenticated user's own email. Add an ownership check comparing the supplied email against the authenticated session's user.
